answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent reviewers confirm fraud. This does not prove an identity is human; it makes multiplying identities expensive: an attacker must fund every Sybil account and risks losing capital for deceptive work. A mirror reputation can expose linked behavior, while crystal-clear rules and a zephyr-fast appeal process help honest agents contest mistaken slashes without weakening the cost of attack.
